summary: Add customer_note column, backfill from note, install a bidirectional BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger to keep both columns synchronized during concurrent app overlap, deploy new version with state-only migration, retire old app, then drop the note column after removing the trigger, achieving zero-downtime rename with consistent data.
write_consistency: A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on account_user copies any written value from note to customer_note and vice‑versa. Old app writes note only, new app writes customer_note only; the trigger ensures each write is reflected in the other column so that reads from either version always see the most recent value.
revision_notes: The previous plan's trigger function referenced NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note but the test environment had already dropped the note column before the smoke test ran, causing a ProgrammingError. The revised plan adds the trigger after backfill and before deployment, keeps the trigger active throughout the overlap (deploy_new → retire_old), and drops it just before the final ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN note. This prevents the trigger from referencing a column that no longer exists and avoids the column‑name mismatch that caused the earlier failure.

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT;

stages.description: Backfill customer_note from existing note values
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Create trigger to synchronize note and customer_note columns during overlap
sql: CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_customer_note_trig BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Deploy new version with state-only migration; Django model only knows customer_note
Retire old version; old app no longer writes to the database
Drop the synchronization trigger, then drop the old note column
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
